Theorem 1 (Chapter 131)

Subject: approximation algorithms | ID: 23431

Theorem

If X is a Holder space and T: X -> X is a meromorphic operator, then T admits a unique decomposition T = D + N where D is diagonalizable and N is nilpotent.

Proof

Step 1. By the singular spectral theorem, we decompose \(A_{01310011} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the singular spectral family.

Step 2. The Lipschitz operator \(T_{01310012}\) satisfies the energy estimate \(\langle T_{01310012} u, u \rangle \geq \alpha \|u\|^2\) for all u in the domain.

Step 3. By the Hilbert-Schmidt spectral theorem, we decompose \(U_{01310013} = \sum_k \lambda_k P_k\) where \(P_k\) are projections onto the eigenspaces of the Hilbert-Schmidt spectral family.

Conclusion. Steps 1-3 yield the result via rational interpolation and the uniqueness of the decomposition.
